anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$
Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: Only a range is given for sigma; the page never says what it denotes (an auxiliary exponent between the saving exponent and lambda).
Big-O notation, covered by the undergraduate asymptotic analysis background.

gaps.note: The outside work is said to add cost, yet it is subtracted; a cost bound should add C(mf)^lambda, so the displayed inequality does not follow from the preceding text.

gaps.quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\lambda<\log_m(s/W)<1$ makes the ratio below 1
gaps.note: The ratio (s/W)/m^lambda is below 1 only when lambda exceeds log_m(s/W), not when it is smaller; this contradicts the later sigma<lambda and the example (0.8>0.585).

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: The kernel, the leaf and the per-chunk handling are never defined, and why the cost is O(f/m^nu) is not given.

gaps.quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
gaps.note: The page cites only the interchange cost and never explains why a row addition costs this or why the outside work is a fixed number of row additions.

gaps.quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
gaps.note: u was a field width in bits; here it silently becomes a number of chunks, and the leaf cost O((s/W)^nu u) is asserted without derivation.
The final inequality to O(f^lambda) is not justified; with f only known to be at least about d^vartheta it does not follow from sigma<lambda alone.
